messages:
Maya (AE): Mike from OrchidHealth is asking about Private Deploy options + egress/allowlist costs. They want to run a POC behind their firewall, need TLS-inspect proxy, and prefer PrivateLink if possible.
Mike_CorpIT: Correct — we need to avoid peering, use interface endpoints. Also need static egress IPs for our allowlist. How does Redwood handle egress IPs and port requirements?
Priya (NetOps): For PrivateLink (interface endpoints) you originate from our infra to cluster egress — we can allocate customer-static EIPs on the connector side so you can whitelist. Ports are typically 443 outbound to Redwood endpoints; if you do TLS-inspect via your proxy you'll still hit 443 to the proxy then to our endpoints.
Sam (Infra Eng): TL;DR: We support two patterns: 1) PrivateLink -> our service endpoint with preserved source when using dedicated NAT/EIP on the connector, 2) Transit/peering for on-prem (not preferred). For Private Deploy (VPC only) we can also support NAT64/44 setups. If you need source IP preservation we recommend the EIP + one-way NAT approach.
Maya (AE): Pricing question from procurement: does Private Deploy + static EIPs add a premium on top of reserved capacity? They asked for ballpark monthly delta.
Sam (Infra Eng): Private Deploy (customer-managed VPC) has enterprise licensing + infra fee. Static EIP assignment itself is just the cloud cost; Redwood charges a connector management fee when we manage the egress HA pair. Ballpark: add ~10-25% on top of base Dedicated commitment depending on HA and support SLAs. I can get a formal quote.
Lena (Security): A couple of compliance notes: if you terminate TLS in your proxy for inspection, you are responsible for cert management and we need to sign an SLA that data at rest is handled per the contract. Also we require mTLS on the connector control plane for Private Deploy.
Mike_CorpIT: For the POC they want to avoid cert churn. Is mutual TLS mandatory or can we do VPN with shared certs for short-term?
Lena (Security): For short-term POC we can provision a time-limited cert with restricted scopes. mTLS on control plane is recommended; we can loosen to IP allowlist + VPN for a trial but will need to harden for production.
Priya (NetOps): Checklist for Mike's infra team: 
• Create interface endpoint in customer VPC for service FQDN(s)
• Configure route table -> endpoint, no route propagation required
• Open outbound 443 to our egress EIP(s) or proxy IPs
• If using TLS-inspect, ensure proxy allows CONNECT to service FQDNs; otherwise we recommend SNI passthrough for session integrity
• Provide ASN and preferred AZ placement for HA pair (we place connectors in multiple AZs)

Sam (Infra Eng): Quick snippet for firewall team (allowlist): 
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood private endpoints
TCP 443 -> 203.0.113.45,203.0.113.46 (example EIPs)
# If using PrivateLink via interface endpoint, allow 10.0.2.0/24 -> endpoint ENIs
```
Maya (AE): I'll send Procurement the high-level delta and ask Sam for a formal quote. Mike — can you share your preferred go-live window and whether the POC needs regional isolation (govcloud)?
Mike_CorpIT: POC target: 6 weeks. We need US-only data residency, no GovCloud for now but strict logging. Also need answers for security questionnaire Q12-Q16 about key management and cert rotation.
Lena (Security): We'll fill out Q12-Q16 — short answers: KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault), customer-managed keys supported for Private Deploy, cert rotation automated for control plane certs but customer rotates TLS leaf certs if terminating at their proxy. I'll DM a skeleton for the questionnaire. :lock: 
Maya (AE): Next steps: Sam to prep quote + EIP count, Priya to share network checklist doc, Lena to send questionnaire skeleton. I'll coordinate POC kickoff with Mike. :thumbsup:
